Q: Grouping stylelint packages with Renovate A:

The configuration block is correct, the issue was the major version difference between package and the activated :separateMultipleMajorReleases. Because of that, Renovate is trying to group but is forced to separate the merge rquest because of the version difference.

We can solve the issue by ensuring no separated release inside the packageRules configuration block like so:

{
  extends: ["packages:stylelint"],
  groupName: "stylelint packages",
  groupSlug: "stylelint",
  separateMajorMinor: false,
  separateMultipleMajor: false,
}

Q: How to run a multinomial logit regression with both individual and time fixed effects in R A:

Here's an ad hoc implementation of femlogit's MATA code intended to follow Chamberlain (1980). As in the MATA implementation, standard ML standard errors are used by default, with optional cluster-robust standard errors. Data can be provided in standard panel-data format.

unique_perms <- function(x) {
  ## helper, calculates unique permutations
  if (length(x) <= 1L) return(matrix(x, nrow=1L))
  vals <- unique(x)
  out <- vector("list", length(vals))
  for (i in seq_along(vals)) {
    z <- vals[i]
    p <- unique_perms(x[-match(z, x)])
    out[[i]] <- cbind(z, p)
  }
  do.call('rbind', out)
}

idx_vec <- function(xg, yg, k, j) {
  ## helper for outcome-specific covariate sums
  out <- matrix(0, nrow=k, ncol=j - 1L)
  keep <- yg > 1L
  if (any(keep)) {
    for (r in which(keep)) out[, yg[r] - 1L] <- out[, yg[r] - 1L] + xg[r, ]
  }
  as.vector(out)
}

prep_panel <- function(ii, yi, x, k, j) {
  ## helper, precomputes indexing before optimization
  xg <- x[ii, , drop=FALSE]
  yg <- yi[ii]
  pp <- unique_perms(yg)
  cvec <- idx_vec(xg, yg, k, j)
  zmat <- t(apply(pp, 1L, \(z) idx_vec(xg, z, k, j)))
  list(cvec=cvec, zmat=zmat)
}

femlogit <- function(formula, id, data, base=NULL, robust=TRUE) {
  ## formula: model formula
  ## id: individual identifier variable
  ## data: input data.frame
  ## base: reference outcome category
  ## robust: sandwich robust SEs
  mf <- model.frame(formula, data=data)
  y <- model.response(mf)
  if (!is.factor(y)) y <- factor(y)
  if (!is.null(base)) y <- relevel(y, ref=base)
  trm <- delete.response(terms(mf))
  x <- model.matrix(trm, mf)
  x <- x[, colnames(x) != "(Intercept)", drop=FALSE]
  yi <- as.integer(y)
  j <- nlevels(y)
  k <- ncol(x)
  q <- k*(j - 1L)
  idx <- split(seq_along(yi), data[[id]])
  panels <- lapply(idx, prep_panel, yi=yi, x=x, k=k, j=j)
  eval_all <- function(par, need_deriv=FALSE) {
    ll <- 0
    s <- matrix(0, nrow=length(panels), ncol=q)
    h <- matrix(0, nrow=q, ncol=q)
    for (g in seq_along(panels)) {
      pg <- panels[[g]]
      z <- drop(pg$zmat %*% par)
      mz <- max(z)
      ez <- exp(z - mz)
      den <- sum(ez)
      w <- ez/den
      ll <- ll + sum(pg$cvec*par) - mz - log(den)
      if (need_deriv) {
        dbar <- drop(crossprod(w, pg$zmat))
        s[g, ] <- pg$cvec - dbar
        ebar <- crossprod(pg$zmat*w, pg$zmat)
        h <- h + tcrossprod(dbar) - ebar
      }
    }
    if (need_deriv) list(value=-ll, score=s, hessian=h) else -ll
  }
  fit <- nlminb(rep(0, q), \(p) eval_all(p))
  ea <- eval_all(fit$par, need_deriv=TRUE)
  b <- matrix(fit$par, nrow=k, ncol=j - 1L)
  rownames(b) <- colnames(x)
  colnames(b) <- levels(y)[-1L]
  bread <- solve(-ea$hessian)
  vc <- bread
  if (robust) {
    meat <- crossprod(ea$score)
    n <- nrow(ea$score)
    vc <- (n/(n - 1L))*bread %*% meat %*% bread
  }
  se <- matrix(sqrt(diag(vc)), nrow=k, ncol=j - 1L)
  rownames(se) <- rownames(b)
  colnames(se) <- colnames(b)
  list(
    coefficients=b,
    se=se,
    vcov=vc,
    hessian=ea$hessian,
    score=ea$score,
    objective=fit$objective,
    convergence=fit$convergence,
    par=fit$par,
    nll=\(p) eval_all(p)
  )
}

Usage

fit_femlogit <- femlogit(
  choice ~ x1 + x2 + factor(time_fixed_effect),
  id="individual_fixed_effect",
  data=df,  ## see OP
  base="a",
  robust=TRUE
)
